fig:fields: Simulated fields for main-test index zero on the periodic $64\times64$ grid: (a) initial condition; (b) the 100-substep comparison reference at $T=0.0035$, with $\epsilon=0.020$ and $M=1$. All grid samples are shown. The common color scale represents the order parameter $\phi$, from $-0.4$ to $0.4$. These panels illustrate the short-time regime and do not constitute a spatial-convergence test.
fig:trajectories: Representative main-test trajectory (index zero) on the legacy periodic $64^2$ grid, with $\epsilon=0.020$, $M=1$ and macro step $10^{-4}$. (a) Area-averaged monitored energy: the 100-substep reference is black with a solid line and circles; the one-substep method is orange with a dashed line and squares; the six-substep residual surrogate is blue with a dotted line and diamonds. (b) Relative field error against the 100-substep reference: one, six and twelve uncorrected substeps use orange dashed squares, teal dash-dot triangles and purple dash-dot-dot pentagons; the residual surrogate uses blue dotted diamonds. The horizontal axis displays $10^3t$. Markers are spaced for legibility; all plotted samples are retained. These are individual trajectories, not ensemble means.
fig:sensitivity: Archived single-trajectory relative field errors $e_{L^2}$ (blue solid circles) and normalized radial structure-factor errors $e_S$ (orange dashed squares), with the fitted filter held fixed. (a) Interface-width sweep at $M=1$. (b) Mobility sweep at $\epsilon=0.020$. Both panels use the same initial field with seed $20260618+300000$, mean zero, the legacy $64^2$ grid and 35 macro steps of length $10^{-4}$. Errors use the 100-substep comparison reference. The nominal point is not the 100-trajectory mean of Table~\ref{tab:accuracy}; no ensemble uncertainty is implied.
fig:newlong: Order-parameter fields for main-test index zero on the legacy periodic $64^2$ collocation grid, with $\epsilon=0.020$ and $M=1$. Panels (a)--(c) show $t=0.035$ and panels (d)--(f) show $t=0.070$. Within each row, left to right: independently refined same-grid ETDRK4 reference, six uncorrected substeps, and the residual surrogate with safeguards. All grid samples are shown on the common blue--white--red $\phi$ scale $[-1.25,1.25]$. The matched ensemble errors are in Table~\ref{tab:long}. These same-grid fields do not establish spatially converged morphology.
fig:cost: Achieved relative field error versus online wall time over $T=0.0035$ on the legacy $64^2$ spatial system, with $\epsilon=0.020$, $M=1$ and a refined ETDRK4 reference. Errors average five initial fields; times average five repetitions per field. Sample standard deviations are in Table~\ref{tab:timing}; no uncertainty bands are implied. Uncorrected propagation uses blue solid circles; fixed ETDRK4, orange dashed squares; adaptive stabilized propagation, teal dash-dot triangles; adaptive ETDRK4, purple dotted diamonds; the residual surrogate, a black pentagon; and piDMD, a red cross. The last two methods each contribute one configuration. The three adaptive ETDRK4 settings have identical errors because the maximum step is reached. Residual timings include correction and acceptance work; fixed ETDRK4 coefficients are warmed before timing.
fig:convergence: Spatial relative field differences against the $512^2$ dealiased ETDRK4 solution after Fourier interpolation of each coarser field, at $\epsilon=0.020$ and $M=1$. Random polynomial case zero uses blue solid circles at $t=0.0035$ and orange dashed squares at $t=0.070$; the deterministic rectangles use teal dash-dot triangles and purple dotted diamonds at the corresponding times. Each point represents one initial field, with no ensemble uncertainty implied. The temporal step is at most $5\times10^{-5}$; time refinement is assessed separately. Table~\ref{tab:convergence} reports adjacent-grid differences, whereas this plot uses $512^2$ as the common comparison grid. Intermediate times and additional random fields are retained in the supplementary data.
fig:rectangles: Order-parameter fields for the smooth periodic two-rectangle test of Eq.~\eqref{eq:rectangles} on the dealiased $256^2$ grid, with $\epsilon=0.020$ and $M=1$: (a) initial field; (b) same-grid ETDRK4 reference at $t=0.070$; (c) six uncorrected substeps at that time; (d) the separately refitted residual surrogate with safeguards at that time. Each displayed cell averages a $4\times4$ block; computations, errors and saved fields retain all $256^2$ samples. All panels use the common $\phi$ scale $[-1.25,1.25]$. This deterministic geometry lies outside the small-amplitude training regime; its errors are reported in Table~\ref{tab:deterministic}.
fig:stress: Diagnostic rollout selected from the separately labeled 12-case exploratory small-step extension on the legacy $64^2$ grid: mean 1, spatial standard deviation 0.08, $\epsilon=0.02$, $M=1$ and macro step $10^{-7}$, with the filter trained at $10^{-4}$. (a) Relative field errors against a time-refined same-grid ETDRK4 reference: safeguarded residual (blue solid circles), unconstrained residual (orange dashed squares), and six uncorrected substeps (teal dash-dot triangles). (b) Accepted fraction $\alpha$ (blue dotted diamonds). All 350 fractions equal $2^{-26}$, nearly freezing the safeguarded field. Markers are spaced for legibility; the saved archive retains every step. This selected case illustrates a failure mode rather than typical performance.
